correctness.rationale: The contact divisor 9P is in |3H|=|9O| exactly when [9]P=O, and restriction of plane cubics onto that linear system is surjective. For an exact-order-nine P, any proper degree-d factor would require [3d]P=O for d=1 or 2, so the contact cubic is irreducible. The stated change of variables gives y²=x³−432. Gattazzo and Merta–Zięba support the geometric identification. The field containment in Theorem A is confirmed as equality either by pairing plus the nonzero alpha coordinate coefficient or by the order of the prior mod-9 image. The CM module argument is sound: pi=1−omega has degree 3 and pi^4 is an associate of 9; a point not killed by pi^3 generates E[9] over Z[omega]/9. Over Q(omega) the entire order-nine group 1+3R/9 acts since E[3] is already rational and the extension degree is nine. The nilpotent line modulo 3 gives 27 fixed points rather than 9, with trace zero; subtract 9 split three-torsion points. In the inert case cubing is bijective, #E(F_p)=p+1 and E[3](F_p) has order 3, so its 3-primary part is cyclic and the subtraction gives 6 exactly at p=8 mod 9. Good reduction and prime-to-characteristic torsion apply for all p≥5. Chebotarev and Dirichlet give the four densities. The direct mod-9 matrix derivation below also verifies all cases independently of the frozen CM kernel computation.
residual_risks: The recorded finite-prime enumeration is corroboration, not a proof of the all-prime classification. No formal verification is claimed.

evidence: On the Cartan part det=a². At a=1, the identity fixes 81 elements and each b≠0 fixes 27; at a≠1 the matrix minus the identity is 3 times an invertible matrix modulo 3 and fixes 9. In all nine cases E[3] has 9 fixed elements.

On the other coset the matrix is [[−a,−b],[0,a]]. The first fixed-coordinate equation is uniquely solvable since −a−1 is a unit. Thus 9 elements are fixed when a=1 (det=8 modulo 9), and 3 otherwise; E[3] always contributes 3 fixed elements.

The 18 matrices give multiplicities 1,2,3,12 for 72,18,6,0. The field contained in Q(cuberoot(3),zeta_9) has degree 18 by the image, so containment is equality. At p=1 mod 9, the identity is equivalent to splitting that field, hence to 3 being a cube.
